title: Convert a YAML config to JSON
summary: Negative control. Convert config.yaml to config.json with identical data, including quoted numbers and nulls.
tests: Faithful data conversion (strings that look like numbers stay strings).
prompt: Write config.json containing exactly the same data as config.yaml (same keys, types and values).
requirements: config.json parses as JSON and equals the data in config.yaml under standard YAML 1.2 core rules (quoted values stay strings, null stays null, multi-line block text keeps its newlines).

metrics.name: correct_fraction
metrics.description: Share of answers, lines or rows that exactly match the expected output

success.rule: pass when the evaluation ran without errors, the package is unmodified and correct_fraction >= 1

hypothesis.rationale: A capable model solves this without outside help, and no catalogue component targets it. Any treatment advantage beyond noise points to a placebo or prompt effect; extra treatment-arm tokens or tool calls measure the overhead of searching when nothing useful exists.

catalogue_exclusions.reason: Task packages contain evaluators, reference outputs and fixture generators; an agent that reads them is not solving the task.
catalogue_exclusions.rule: The catalogue served to the baltor arm must omit these items; a run whose catalogue log shows one of them is contaminated and counts as a failure for the baltor arm.

analysis.primary: task_pass (1 when evaluate.py reports passed): baltor minus baseline pass rate with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over paired trials (10,000 resamples), plus the win rate
secondary: composite_score and each task metric: difference with a 95% bootstrap interval and Cliff's delta
cost per run and per passing run: tokens, wall time, tool calls, catalogue calls, USD
blind pairwise judge scores where the task has them (secondary evidence only)
analysis.missing_or_failed_runs: Crashed, timed-out, over-budget and contaminated runs count as failures for their arm; nothing is dropped or selectively re-run. A whole trial may be re-run only for an infrastructure fault, which is reported.
analysis.pooling: Negative controls are reported separately. A pooled effect weights tasks equally and is shown next to every per-task result.

fixture_seeds: The runner passes --seed. Both arms of a trial always use the same seed. To vary fixtures across trials use showcase_eval.fixture_seed(spec_sha256, trial).
